reviews.comment: Dr. Birchfield is a caring professor that cares about his students and his subject. His power systems stability course had some quite difficult homework assignments, but these were graded generously if a good attempt was made. The exams less difficult in comparison to the homework. Felt like I learned a lot!

Waited to graduate and post this review. Useless and old material. rudimentary knowledge about the concepts which are related to 20 years ago. I strongly recommend that all students be more cautious. You won't benefit from this course. Neither the course material, the teaching style, nor the credit. He thinks he is funny, but no, he's not.

Birchfield is a really fun lecturer and is knowledgeable about power systems. His exams are a bit on the easier side for some reason, and he covers just enough of the material (I felt he could have gone deeper than he did). But one thing is for sure, he enjoys teaching, and that is enough to make you feel excited about the class and eager to learn

I took Birchfield's 460 class. He's a young professor and very knowledgeable in power systems. He even co-authored on the latest edition of the textbook. Half of the exam problems are short answer over concepts.  Quiz almost every class but it's not hard if you follow his slides. Lab software is cool and the lab's don't require much thinking.
Quizzes nearly every lecture; lectures were pretty thorough and easy to understand; gave us pretty good review material
I had Birchfield for ECEN 214. He was great, and I highly recommend that you pick this teacher!
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Birchfield's class could be a little slow at times, as others have mentioned, but his class was one of the best I've taken in a while. To sum it up, the class felt fair. He was upfront about what he wanted you to learn and he provided all the necessary resources and more for anyone to succeed. TIP: Study the sample problems, HW, & book!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell he's a good, nice guy, new to teaching. Lectures a tad boring but most classes are. Homework is optional, but study hw & quiz solutions and review lecture concepts & you'll be good for test. No curveballs on test. Very lenient grader in my opinion, test averages were high B. Labs arent too bad, leniency in grades depends on TA.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a little dry and sometimes example problems need more clarity (he addresses this occasionally with some videos). I thought he was lenient on grading exams, they usually structured with some sort of short response based off lectures/slides and workout problems (homework, example slides etc). Dropped a few quizzes as well.

The class wasn't that bad. Honestly pretty mediocre, but his quizzes were essentially just the examples from lecture or the homeworks (which he gives solutions to). His tests aren't that bad since you are given one cheat sheet, and it is somewhat similar to quizzes/homework. Lectures are just him reading the slides, so its kind of boring.

I mean, it's his first semester but dude. All he does is read slides in a neutral voice. He didn't do hardly ANY workout problems which meant all the material had to be self taught. Not bad I guess just aggressively mediocre. At least none of the homework is for a grade, but that might just be because he has no grader.
